claims.text: Al is an oxide-forming element suitable for use as a coating.
A thin Al coating can improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed protection applies to unloaded exposure in air at 800 °C for 5 h.
The coating will form a protective oxide layer on equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The oxide-forming coating reacts with oxygen to produce the protective layer.
The protective layer prevents or limits reaction between oxygen and the underlying alloy.
Limiting oxygen reaction with the underlying alloy reduces oxidation relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coated alloy will have improved oxygen resistance relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating may improve the alloy's high-temperature mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: Mechanical-property improvement is described only as potential and its impact as uncertain, yet the falsification rule states that lack of improvement in either oxidation resistance or mechanical properties falsifies the hypothesis. Thus, failure to improve mechanical properties alone could nominally falsify a claim that was not made decisively.
